newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's GDP to grow 3.0-4.0 pct in 1997-minister.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's GDP to grow 3.0-4.0 pct in 1997-minister.

text.p: Morocco's gross domestic product should grow between 3.0 and 4.0 percent this year against 11.8 percent in 1996, Minister of Population Lamine Ben Omar said on Monday.

"According to the updated figures we have, the Moroccan economy is expected to grow by an average three to four percent this year compared with 11.8 percent in 1996," Ben Omar told a news conference held at headquarters of his departement in Rabat.
He said the record agricultural harvest drove last year's strong growth compared with minus 7.6 percent in 1995.

"Morocco harvested 100 million quintals (10 million tonnes) in 1996, a revised figure from 97.5 million quintals announced earlier...The agricultural sector added value rose 76 percent to 22.6 billion dirhams ($2.5 billion) in 1996," Ben Omar said.
Agriculture's added value was 12.8 billion dirhams in 1995, he said.
The sector represents more than 20 percent of Morocco's GDP, analysts said.
"The economy evolved last year in an environment in which the inflation remained under tight control...The inflation was 3.0 percent in 1996, the lowest level since 1988," the minister said.
He said the inflation was 6.1 percent in 1995.
Ben Omar said, despite the complexity of the phenomena of unemployment, the number of jobless in urban areas fell to 18.5 percent in 1996 from 23 percent the previous year.
Unemployment in rural areas was not available.
Morocco has an estimated 10 million workforce, of which 50 percent is located in rural areas.

The minister said a government detailed survey on the population in Morocco's 1,545 urban and rural municipalities will be issued in coming months to give analysts a clear picture of the country's emerging economy.
